scene: Day 90, hilltop: Reed (blue-gray scarf, gray backpack) and Mara (purple forearm band, teal pack) stand inside a round dry-stone sheepfold, ringed on the grass by a band of pale light with one narrow gap. A single glowing circle marker, with no partner, sits beside the gap. Just beyond it stand the Worker (plain mint-headed alien, closed silver case) and the Surveyor (mint head, blue shoulder stripe, scanner lowered). The ship's dark straight-edged slab fills the whole sky overhead, and a radio mast stands on the far ridge. What makes it scary: the gap is only wide enough for one, and Mara is staring at it instead of at Reed.

Day 72, at dawn, in a grassy field beside a canal: Reed and Mara lie flat in a ditch with empty hands. The Surveyor's pale scanner beam has passed straight through the green narrowboat behind them and stopped on Reed's back. The Surveyor has stepped off the towpath toward them while the Worker kneels on the path, setting down a glowing joined-circle marker. What makes it scary: the beam ignores the bags and the tin and finds the people, and for the first time an alien is walking straight at them.
